monadnock-building.what: An early office skyscraper whose two halves demonstrate the transition from load-bearing masonry to a metal frame.
monadnock-building.history: Burnham & Root's north half opened in 1891. Holabird & Roche added the south half in 1893.
architecture: At the north end, look at the thick brick base, projecting bays and curved cornice without applied ornament.
The south half has more conventional decorative brick and terra cotta; its façade hangs from a metal frame.
The north half also uses hidden metal structure: it is not a building made exclusively of load-bearing brick.
visit: The exterior is the reliable visit. Unrestricted tourist access and lobby hours are not confirmed.
Compare the two halves while walking along Dearborn Street.

rookery-light.what: Burnham & Root's office building with a central Light Court remodelled by Frank Lloyd Wright.
rookery-light.history: Completed in 1888. Wright remodelled the Light Court in 1905; William Drummond made further changes in 1931.
architecture: The roof glazing brings daylight into the centre of the deep office block.
Wright encased the existing iron columns in white marble with gilded ornament and introduced bronze light fittings.
Look up to the curved oriel staircase; access beyond the ground-floor lobby depends on the tour.
visit: Free first-floor lobby access is published Monday–Friday 07:00–18:00 and Saturday 08:00–14:00, via Adams Street.
A guided tour is optional for the lobby visit. No tour ticket is currently supplied.

federal-center.what: A federal complex comprising the Dirksen Courthouse, Kluczynski Federal Building and Loop Post Office around a public plaza.
federal-center.history: Built between 1960 and 1974 with Mies van der Rohe as chief designer, working with three other architectural practices. Alexander Calder's Flamingo stands in the plaza.
architecture: Projecting black I-beam mullions give the glass elevations their repeated vertical rhythm.
Compare the two tall blocks with the low post office pavilion and the open space between them.
Granite paving and the regular structural grid tie the separate buildings together.
visit: The itinerary visits the public plaza.
Courthouse access involves identification and security screening; it is not an unrestricted architecture-tour interior.

marquette.what: An early Chicago School office building with an ornate public lobby and a Native-led installation in its arcade.
marquette.history: Holabird & Roche completed the building in 1895. It is now the MacArthur Foundation's headquarters.
architecture: Tiffany glass mosaics and bronze reliefs decorate the lobby.
The ornament tells a colonial account of Jacques Marquette; the installation Nwi Yathmomen, We will tell our story addresses it from Indigenous perspectives.
visit: The owner publishes lobby access daily 07:00–19:00, with rare exceptions.
The installation is on the ground floor; no museum ticket is listed.

caa-hotel.what: A former private athletic club, now a hotel, with public Drawing Room dining beside Millennium Park.
caa-hotel.history: Henry Ives Cobb designed the club, which opened in 1893. It was restored and reopened as a hotel in 2015.
architecture: The Michigan Avenue façade takes its Venetian Gothic cues from the Doge's Palace.
In the Drawing Room, look at the restored 1890s woodwork and three fireplaces.
The former athletic spaces remain legible in the hotel's Game Room and former pool area.
visit: Use the Drawing Room for the planned interior-and-lunch stop; seating is subject to availability.
The public lobby is accessible independently of staying at the hotel.

bean.what: Cloud Gate, Anish Kapoor's polished stainless-steel public sculpture in Millennium Park.
bean.history: Unveiled with Millennium Park in 2004. Kapoor's studio lists the work as 2004.
architecture: The curved mirror surface compresses the skyline, park and people into one reflection.
Walk beneath the concave underside to see how the reflections change.
Its welded steel plates are polished so their seams are not visible.
visit: The sculpture is an outdoor stop; no museum ticket is required.
Approach through Millennium Park, across Michigan Avenue from the Athletic Association.

cultural-center.what: Chicago's former central public library, now a free cultural venue.
cultural-center.history: Completed in 1897 by Shepley, Rutan & Coolidge. The building became the Chicago Cultural Center after the main library moved to the Harold Washington Library in 1991.
architecture: Preston Bradley Hall contains the Tiffany glass dome, approximately 38 feet across.
Compare the glass dome in the Grand Army of the Republic rooms with the Tiffany dome.
Look at the marble staircases, mosaic surfaces and inscriptions within the restrained limestone exterior.
visit: Published hours are daily 10:00–17:00; self-guided entry is free.

Published visiting hours are daily 10:00–17:00. The museum is beside the Cultural Center; it is not in the current numbered itinerary.

crown-hall.what: Mies van der Rohe's building for Illinois Tech's architecture school, still used for teaching.
crown-hall.history: Completed in 1956. Virgil Abloh studied architecture at Illinois Tech; his connection is to the school and campus, not authorship of this building.
architecture: Four large external steel girders suspend the roof, leaving the principal studio floor without interior columns.
Compare the translucent lower glazing with the transparent upper panes.
The raised main floor and south stair turn the entrance into a broad platform.
visit: The interior is a priority, but visitor permission for 30 October has not been confirmed.

mtcc.what: Illinois Tech's student centre by Rem Koolhaas and OMA, directly beneath the elevated railway.
mtcc.history: Completed in 2003, the project reconnects the campus's two sides within Mies van der Rohe's earlier masterplan.
architecture: The railway passes through a large noise-reducing steel tube above the building.
The low campus centre contains a mixture of dining, meeting, study and other student spaces.
This is an OMA building by Koolhaas, not a Mies building.
visit: Pair the exterior with Crown Hall on the IIT campus.

robie-house.history: Completed in 1910. Wright personally opposed demolition threats in 1941 and 1957; the Trust completed a major interior restoration in 2019.
architecture: Long roof cantilevers, terraces and brick-and-limestone bands emphasise the horizontal.
The main living and dining areas share one long space around a central chimney.
Look at the repeated diagonal and diamond patterns in the leaded-glass windows.

unity-temple.history: Commissioned in 1905 and dedicated in September 1909. It is one of the eight Wright works on the UNESCO World Heritage List.
architecture: The plain concrete exterior contrasts with the warm wood, colour and geometry of the sanctuary.
A low entrance sequence opens into a taller worship space.
Clerestory windows and 25 amber-tinted skylights bring light in above eye level.

home-studio.what: Frank Lloyd Wright's own Oak Park home and the adjoining office where his practice developed the Prairie style.
home-studio.history: Wright built the house in 1889, added the children's playroom in 1895 and the studio wing in 1898. He lived and worked here until 1909.
architecture: The house uses a large triangular gable, window bays and a curved veranda as simple geometric forms.
The playroom has a barrel-vaulted ceiling, leaded glass and a skylight screened by wooden grilles.
Compare the low reception area with the studio's taller drafting room.

architecture: Two colours of Roman brick form alternating projecting bands across the façade.
A broad hipped roof, deep eaves and a continuous upper window band reinforce the horizontal.
The entrance sits beneath a substantial round arch; the principal living rooms are upstairs.

mca-museum.history: Josef Paul Kleihues's present building opened in 1996. Johnston Marklee redesigned public areas in 2017. Virgil Abloh: Figures of Speech was a past exhibition, not a current show promised for this trip.
architecture: The façade pairs cast aluminium with an Indiana limestone base.
Kleihues carried a square grid through the elevations and floor plans.
The 2017 changes added public gathering spaces and Marisol without enlarging the building footprint.

architecture: The towers stand at right angles, opening views toward Lake Michigan.
A repeated steel-and-glass grid runs across their façades.
Look at the relationship between the open ground level, columns and lakefront setting.

ginos.history: Founded in 1966 by Sam Levine, Fred Bartoli and George Loverde. Cook Alice Mae Redmond developed the dough recipe associated with Gino's East.

art-institute.what: An art museum combining the historic Michigan Avenue building with Renzo Piano’s Modern Wing, with collections from many periods and regions.
art-institute.history: The Michigan Avenue building opened in 1893, designed by Shepley, Rutan & Coolidge. Renzo Piano Building Workshop’s Modern Wing was completed in 2009.
architecture: Compare the original Beaux-Arts building with the Modern Wing’s glass-and-metal façade and limestone panels, which echo the older building.
The Modern Wing’s “flying carpet” roof uses curved aluminium blades to filter daylight into its upper galleries.
Griffin Court is the double-height entrance hall. The Nichols Bridgeway crosses Monroe Street to connect the museum with Millennium Park.
visit: Main entrance: 111 S Michigan Avenue. Modern Wing entrance: 159 E Monroe Street. Individual collection highlights may be off view.
